page: Google Cloud Platform e2-highcpu-16 is a compute-skewed virtual machine within the general-purpose E2 instance family. It is provisioned with 16 dedicated vCPUs based on 8 physical cores from an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.2 GHz using the x86_64 architecture. The system provides 16.0 GB of memory, equating to an allocation of 1.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Cache resources include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of shared L3 cache. There are no bundled GPUs or local storage disks included with the instance, requiring network-attached storage for non-volatile data persistence.

Benchmark evaluations reveal middling overall throughput alongside distinct single-thread limitations. The instance reached an average multi-core Geekbench score of 5488.0 and a PassMark CPU rating of 12431.07, while stress-ng recorded 21496.93 in multi-core metrics. Conversely, single-core execution tests such as Geekbench single-core at 858.0, text processing at 1154.0, and gzip compression at 18.89 GB/sec fall into the lowest performance decile. CPU instruction set extensions include standard AVX, AES, and bit-manipulation primitives (BMI2, ADX, FMA), but lack AVX-512 extensions and AMX accelerator support.

Memory bandwidth benchmarks register 71.67 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 35.27 GB/sec for writes, resulting in an average PassMark memory score of 2051.68. Real-world services show consistent mid-tier execution, including Redis throughput achieving 15.91 million SET operations per second and static web serving throughput hitting 12.91 GB/sec. Small-model LLM inference benchmarks delivered 904.78 tokens per second on prompt processing and 209.07 tokens per second on generation.

Cost efficiency for the e2-highcpu-16 derives from offering a high count of dedicated compute threads at lower RAM allocations. This structure favors applications that require raw CPU concurrency without high memory capacities. The primary architectural tradeoff is the constrained single-threaded performance and the 1:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The instance is suited for parallelized compilation, batch data transformation, microservices serving, and concurrent stateless web application workloads.
description: Google Cloud Platform e2-highcpu-16 is an x86_64 general-purpose compute instance equipped with 16 vCPUs (8 physical cores) powered by a 2.2 GHz Intel Xeon processor. It includes 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a 1:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1.0 GB per core, with no bundled GPUs or local disk storage. Benchmark testing positions the instance within the mid-range for multi-threaded tasks, logging 21496.93 on multi-core stress-ng, 5488.0 in Geekbench multi-core, and 15.91 million Redis SET operations per second. However, single-core throughput remains low, with Geekbench single-core scoring 858.0 and gzip compression registering in the bottom 10%. With hardware support for AVX and AES but absent AVX-512, this server provides a balanced resource tier for concurrent workloads that do not demand large memory footprints, such as multi-threaded compilation, batch data transformations, and stateless web application servers.
